Protected paths. https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/dangerous-directories-Thunderbird-account-settings Please right click the "Local Folders" account and check that the path in Settings is as shown in your post. I am just a little perturbed that the first part is showing as a UNC path with the \\

2. Password issues on ATT. That is about as vanilla as it gets around here, for reasons best understood by ATT you need to use a mailkey you get from their website, not your ATT password, to retreive email.

Recent changes mean that oAuth authentication can also be used with ATT, but I am not sure if they have arrived at a release version as yet. If it is an option use it instead of a password.

Note that "Server error" part is usually reported by folk using their ATT password for mail instead of a mailkey when asked for their password.

content:
Let's start by defining the "write formatting toolbar".

my reading of that is you are not seeing the toolbar with font names and sizes that appears between the addressing part of the new email and the body text. If I am wrong please clarify.

This toolbar is only visible in normal circumstances if you are composing your email in HTML. So the first "test" is to hold the shift key and click to open a new compose window. That will toggle the compose setting. If it is set to HTML it will make it plain text and vice versa for that click only.

Composition in HTML is a per account setting so while some of your accounts may be set to HTML, perhaps not all of them are. If Thunderbird is selecting the one that is not set to HTML as the default to use you will think there is a problem.
